why: The vocabulary agrees: B's Cnum is the project's critCount by rfl (ncard of {critical, index = λ}). A (finsum_neg_one_pow_indexM_eq_sum_critCount) is the regrouping identity Σ_{p critical} (-1)^{ind p} = Σ_{λ ≤ dim} (-1)^λ C_λ for any f with finitely many critical points on any charted space. B instead asserts that, for a smooth function with non-degenerate critical points on a compact manifold, the critical set (and each index class) is finite and C_λ = 0 for λ > dim, so the alternating sums end at ±C_n. A ⇒ B is proved only because B holds outright from project lemmas outside the item (IsMorseFunction.finite_setOf_isCriticalPointM, indexM_le_finrank); A contributes nothing. B ⇒ A fails for lack of content: the regrouping identity, which A states for arbitrary spaces, is not in B. Both say 'the sums stop at C_n', but each has content the other lacks.
